readme:
# Resident Advisor Events Scraper

Collect event listings from Resident Advisor for one or more cities and a date range. Each row is one event with its title, times, venue and address, lineup, promoters, genres, price text, flyer image and attendance numbers. You pay per event delivered.

The data comes from the public event pages of [Resident Advisor](https://ra.co/). No account and no API key are needed. Only event data is collected, no user data.

## What you get

For each event the actor returns one row with:

- `id`, `url`, `title`: the event and its page on Resident Advisor
- `date`, `startTime`, `endTime`: the day and the times in local time at the venue (no time zone offset)
- `listingDate`: the day the event is listed under. Events that run over several days can be listed on more than one day
- `description`: the event text written by the promoter
- `cost`: the price text shown on the event page, for example `15-25`. It is empty for many events
- `isTicketed`, `ticketUrl`, `minimumAge`, `isFestival`
- `flyerImage` and `images`
- `attending` and `interestedCount`: the counts shown on the event page
- `artists`: the acts that have a profile on Resident Advisor, each with `id`, `name`, `url` and `room` (the room or stage heading the act is listed under, such as `Room 01`, or null)
- `lineupText`: the full lineup as plain text, one line per entry, as the source shows it. It holds acts without a profile, b2b notes and marks such as (live)
- `lineupNames`: the lines of the lineup that are not profile acts, each line as written and not split. Headings and lines without two letters are left out
- `promoters`: `id`, `name` and `url`
- `genres`: genre names
- `venue`: `id`, `name`, `address` and `url`
- `area` and `country`: the city area and country of the venue
- `editorsPick`: the pick text, when the event has one
- `scrapedAt`

A value the source does not show is null. Lists with nothing in them are empty.

## Typical uses

- Build a calendar of club nights and festivals for a city
- Find which promoters and venues are busy in a given week
- Follow the lineups of specific genres across several cities
- Feed a newsletter, a map, a booking tool or a spreadsheet with fresh listings

## Pricing

You pay per event delivered, plus a small fee for each run.

| Event | Name | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Run start (charged once, together with the first delivered row) | `actor-start` | $0.001 per run |
| One event row | `event-result` | $0.0025 per event ($2.50 per 1,000) |

A run that finds nothing is not charged. If you set a maximum cost for the run, the actor stops cleanly once the next row would go over it.

**New to Apify?** Every account gets a $5 free monthly platform credit, enough for a first test run before you pay anything.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `areas` | list | `London` | City names such as `London`, `Berlin`, `New York`, `Ibiza`, or area ids such as `13` |
| `startDate` | text | today | First day, like `2026-11-20` |
| `endDate` | text | 14 days after the start date | Last day, like `2026-11-30` |
| `genres` | list | empty | Keep only these genres, for example `techno` or `tech house`. Empty keeps all |
| `maxItems` | number | 100 | Maximum events in total, up to 10,000 |

How it works:

- Common cities (London, Berlin, Amsterdam, New York, Paris, Barcelona, Ibiza, Manchester, Los Angeles, Tokyo) are known to the actor. Other names are looked up on Resident Advisor and the closest match is used. If the wrong city is picked, the log shows the area used, and you can give its area id instead.
- With several areas and several genres, the actor reads one page of each in turn, so a small `maxItems` still covers every area.
- Each page holds up to 50 events.
- Events are removed when they appear twice, for example in two areas.
- Number fields also accept numbers written as text, for example `"50"`.
- Started with no input, the actor returns a sample of upcoming London events.

### Example: London this week

```json
{
  "areas": ["London"],
  "startDate": "2026-11-20",
  "endDate": "2026-11-27",
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

### Example: two cities, techno only

```json
{
  "areas": ["Berlin", "Amsterdam"],
  "genres": ["techno"],
  "maxItems": 200
}
```

## Limitations

- The actor reads what Resident Advisor shows publicly. Events that are not listed there are not in the data.
- `cost` is the text the promoter typed. Many events leave it empty, and it can hold a range or a currency sign only. There are no ticket tiers.
- `ticketUrl` is the event page, where Resident Advisor shows the ticket link. The final ticket seller address is not part of the data.
- Times are local times at the venue. There is no time zone offset.
- `lineupNames` is a best-effort list. A line can hold several acts, for example `A b2b B`, and it is kept whole.
- `genres` is empty for events without genre tags.
- `attending` and `interestedCount` change often. A row shows the values at `scrapedAt`.
- The genre filter takes the genre name, for example `techno`, `house`, `tech house` or `drum and bass`. Spaces, hyphens and capitals do not matter. A name the source does not know gives no rows.
- Very large cities can list more events than `maxItems`. Narrow the date range or raise `maxItems`.
- If the source keeps refusing, the run stops with a status that says so, and only delivered rows are charged.

## FAQ

**Do I need a Resident Advisor account?**
No. The actor reads public event pages.

**How do I find an area id?**
Type the city name in `areas`. The actor finds the id itself. The log shows which area was used.

**Why did I get fewer rows than `maxItems`?**
The areas, dates and genres hold fewer events, or the maximum cost you set for the run was reached. The run status message says which.

**Why are some `cost` values empty?**
The promoter did not enter a price. The field is null then.

**Can one event show up twice?**
No. Rows are unique by event id within a run.

**Can a run be restarted safely?**
Yes. Progress is saved after every page. A restarted run continues where it stopped and does not deliver or charge the same rows twice.

**Is this affiliated with Resident Advisor?**
No. This is an independent tool that reads public data. Please keep your use modest and in line with the terms of the source.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex.

**MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=nanodata/resident-advisor-events-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `resident-advisor-events-scraper` to list electronic music events in Berlin next weekend with venue and lineup. Return results as a table."

Found a problem or need a field added? Open an issue on the [Issues tab](https://apify.com/nanodata/resident-advisor-events-scraper/issues). We usually reply within one business day. You can also email contact@nanoscrape.com.
